deed: Waldemar Haffkine was the first to develop vaccines against cholera and plague, and saved lives in India
title: Haffkine's Cholera and Plague Vaccines in India

trailer.text: Waldemar Mordecai Haffkine was a bacteriologist who developed a vaccine against cholera and a vaccine against plague.
Waldemar Mordecai Haffkine, after whom the Haffkine Institute in Bombay is named, was born in Odessa in 1860 to a Jewish family.
In 1892 he reported in Paris that a vaccine against cholera had protected guinea pigs, and he vaccinated himself with it.
In 1893 he arrived in India, and according to his own report he vaccinated more than 42,000 people there against cholera by 1895.
When plague reached Bombay in 1896, the Government of India asked him to develop a vaccine against it as well.
Between 1897 and 1925, 26 million doses of his plague vaccine were sent out from Bombay.

paragraphs.text: Waldemar Mordecai Haffkine was born in Odessa, Ukraine, on 15 March 1860.
His parents were Aaron and Rosalie Chavkin, née Landsberg.
It was a Jewish family of merchants, educated in Western culture.
These were times of unrest, repression and pogroms.
Haffkine became a political activist and joined the Odessa League of Self Defence.
In 1884 he completed studies in zoology at the University of Odessa.
He was denied a professorship because he was a Jew.
He was offered a teaching position on condition that he convert to Christianity, and he refused.
In 1889 Metchnikoff offered him the only vacant position at the Pasteur Institute: librarian.

stations.title: Vaccine in guinea pigs, then in himself

paragraphs.text: An earlier attempt by Ferrán in Valencia to vaccinate against cholera was not adopted in other countries, and was discontinued in Spain.
Haffkine wanted to develop an effective vaccine against Asiatic cholera in humans.
He discovered that passing cholera bacteria repeatedly through the abdominal cavity of guinea pigs produced a more virulent culture.
On 9 July 1892 he reported to the Society of Biology in Paris: an injection of attenuated bacteria, followed by one of exalted bacteria, immunized guinea pigs against cholera.
The immunity he saw in animals convinced him that the vaccine would also work in humans, and he vaccinated himself.
According to the BBC, on 18 July 1892 he risked his life and injected himself with attenuated cholera.
In 1893 Lord Dufferin, Britain's ambassador in Paris and a former Viceroy of India, suggested that he travel to Bengal.
According to the Dictionary of Scientific Biography, Haffkine first wanted to test the vaccine in an epidemic in Siam.
The Secretary of State for India permitted him to visit all parts of India, on condition that all injections be voluntary.
He arrived in India in March 1893 and hoped to begin in Calcutta.
But cholera was not a problem there at the time, and he met local opposition.
Some doctors believed that an injection under the skin would not protect against a disease of the digestive system.
According to the Dictionary of Scientific Biography, when a crowd threw stones, Haffkine pulled up his shirt and let another doctor insert a syringe into his side.
He chose to work with Indian doctors and assistants rather than with British ones.
In the Katal Bagan neighbourhood in Calcutta he vaccinated 116 of about 200 residents.
Afterwards there were 10 more cases in the neighbourhood, seven of them fatal, all among those who had not been vaccinated.

In the trial in Calcutta, cholera broke out in 36 houses in which inoculated people lived. In these houses, among 335 who were not inoculated there were 45 cases and 39 deaths, and among 181 inoculated there were four cases and four deaths, but according to the source the numbers were too small to draw a clear conclusion from them.
According to Prof. Chakrabarti, after the initial opposition people queued for a whole day in the slums of Calcutta to be vaccinated.
By the end of the first year, about 10,000 British and Indian soldiers had been vaccinated.
According to his own records, that year he vaccinated about 23,000 people in northern India.

In 1915 the statisticians Greenwood and Yule examined eight results and found that in three of them the reduction in the number of attacks in the inoculated relative to the uninoculated created a strong presumption in favour of Haffkine's vaccine, while in the other results the reduction could have arisen by chance from sampling errors.
In late September 1896 plague reached Bombay.
At first the British government played down the severity of the outbreak, so that the port would stay open for business.
The plague raged through the crowded slums, and its mortality rate was nearly twice that of cholera.
The Government of India, impressed by the cholera vaccine, asked Haffkine to develop a similar vaccine against plague.
He was given a small room and a corridor, one clerk and three untrained assistants.
On 10 January 1897 he injected himself with 10 cc of the preparation, much more than the 3 cc planned for wide use.
He began his work in a room in the Petit Laboratory of Grant Medical College in Bombay.
According to the BBC, at Byculla jail there were 12 cases and six deaths among the untreated, and two cases and no deaths among the treated.
In the village of Undhera, among 71 vaccinated people there were eight cases and three deaths, and among 64 unvaccinated people there were 27 cases and 26 deaths.
The Aga Khan, a spiritual leader, placed a lodge at his disposal and volunteered to be vaccinated together with thousands of members of his community.

After the protection that the vaccine appeared to give in the trial at Byculla jail at the end of January 1897 became known, more than 11,000 people in the infected areas were inoculated in the following three months.

stations.title: A laboratory, an institute and millions of doses

paragraphs.text: In 1897 Queen Victoria named Haffkine a Companion of the Order of the Indian Empire, and in 1899 he received British citizenship.
According to a website, on 10 August 1899 the mansion at Parel, which had once been the residence of the Governor of Bombay, was formally handed over to him.
In December 1901 he was appointed Director-in-Chief of the Plague Research Laboratory, with a staff of 53 people.
Between 1897 and 1925, 26 million doses of his plague vaccine were sent out from Bombay.
Tests showed a reduction of 50% to 85% in mortality among the vaccinated.
In 1925, in tribute, the Bombay Government renamed the laboratory the Haffkine Institute.
In 1900 he received the Cameron Prize in Practical Therapeutics from the University of Edinburgh.
In 1909 the French Academy of Sciences awarded him the Prix Bréant for his achievements in preventive vaccination against cholera and plague.
On 16 March 1964 India's postal department announced a stamp in his memory.
According to Prof. Chakrabarti, Haffkine was the first to bring this kind of laboratory medicine to a tropical country like India.
According to the epidemiologist Lahariya, it must never be forgotten that he made a viable vaccine in a two-room laboratory with a very small team.
According to the encyclopedia entry written by Edith Lutzker, Haffkine was an observant Jew for most of his life.
He participated actively in the efforts of Jewish organizations to create an independent Jewish state in Palestine.
In 1929 he founded the Haffkine Foundation in Lausanne.
According to a website, the foundation was intended to encourage young talents in Jewish religious schools in Eastern Europe.
He died in Lausanne in October 1930.
In Mulkowal in Punjab, 19 people died of tetanus after being vaccinated against plague on 30 October 1902.
According to Hawgood, all the dead had received vaccine from one bottle, 53N, which had come from the Bombay laboratory.
The other 88 people, who had received vaccine from other bottles, were unaffected.
According to the Dictionary of Scientific Biography, Haffkine was suspended without pay even before proper investigations had begun.
The Commission of Inquiry, headed by Sir Lawrence Jenkins, chief justice of Bombay, also included Major David Semple, Director of the Pasteur Institute at Kasauli.
The commission found that Haffkine had changed production procedures previously approved by the Plague Commission.
It viewed the omission of carbolic acid with extreme gravity.
On the other hand, it was found that the vaccinator's assistant at Mulkowal had dropped the forceps on the ground and had not properly sterilized them before opening the bottle.
Ronald Ross and Simpson began a campaign to clear Haffkine of blame.
At the height of the campaign, on 29 July 1907, a letter signed by ten distinguished bacteriologists was published in The Times.
Ross wrote in Nature in 1907 that blaming the laboratory caused the people to reject the vaccine, and perhaps the loss of thousands of lives from plague.

In a letter to The Times of 15 March 1907, Ross wrote that if the end of the affair did not change, it would convict India and her rulers of indifference to science, stupidity, injustice, and gross ingratitude to one of their greatest benefactors.
After he was cleared, Haffkine returned to India as Director-in-Chief of the Biological Laboratory in Calcutta.

After his return he was barred from carrying out vaccine trials, and his repeated requests to the Government of India to conduct such trials were rejected, so that he was limited to theoretical research.
In March 1915, on reaching the retirement age of 55, he left the Indian Civil Service and India.

versions.says: According to a website, he was a victim of antisemitism several times, from Tsarist Russia to British India

According to Eli Chernin, it is not evident from the archives that Haffkine was an overt victim of anti-Semitism, but in his words it would be naive to think that the Edwardian bureaucracy was not influenced at all by his being Jewish.

disagreements.question: How many people did Haffkine vaccinate against cholera?

versions.says: Haffkine reported that he vaccinated more than 42,000 people between April 1893 and the end of July 1895
According to the Dictionary of Scientific Biography, within two years 45,000 people were vaccinated and mortality from cholera fell by 70 percent

disagreements.question: How many prisoners were vaccinated at Byculla jail?

versions.says: According to Hawgood's article, 154 prisoners who volunteered were vaccinated
According to the BBC, 147 prisoners were vaccinated and 172 were left untreated

disagreements.question: How much money did Haffkine give to the foundation?

versions.says: According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, he bequeathed $500,000 to the foundation
According to a website, he donated all his property as well as $300,000

disagreements.question: On what date did Haffkine die?

versions.says: According to the Dictionary of Scientific Biography, on 25 October 1930
According to the Kyiv Post, on 26 October 1930, in a hotel room

disagreements.question: How many days passed between the preparation of bottle 53N and its use?

versions.says: According to Hawgood, the bottle was issued from the Bombay laboratory 26 days earlier
According to the BBC, the bottle was prepared 41 days earlier at the Parel laboratory

disagreements.question: Was Haffkine observant all his life, or did he turn to religion only later?

versions.says: According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica entry by Edith Lutzker: he was an observant Jew most of his life
According to Hawgood's article: his upbringing had little religious training, and only over the years did he become increasingly devoted to the Jewish religion
According to the BBC: in his later life he devoted himself to his faith, becoming increasingly orthodox

unknowns.text: The claims do not say that Haffkine was the first in the world to develop a vaccine against cholera; it is known only that an earlier attempt by Ferrán in Valencia was not adopted
It is not known how many lives in total were saved by the vaccines; only the numbers of people vaccinated and the results of certain trials are known

claims.text: לדברי פרופ' צ'קרבארטי, האפקין היה הראשון שהביא רפואת מעבדה כזו למדינה טרופית כמו הודו.
claims.quote: Haffkine was the first person who brought that kind of laboratory medicine into a tropical country like India

claims.text: לדברי האפידמיולוג לאהריה, אסור לשכוח שהאפקין יצר חיסון בר-קיימא במעבדה בת שני חדרים עם צוות קטן מאוד.
claims.quote: We should never forget that Haffkine made a viable vaccine in a two-room lab with a very small team. It is almost unbelievable.

claims.text: האפקין, יהודי שומר מצוות רוב חייו, הקים ב-1929 את קרן האפקין בלוזאן והוריש לה הון של 500,000 דולר.
claims.quote: in 1929 he created the Haffkine Foundation in Lausanne, bequeathing to it his fortune of $500,000

claims.text: האפקין השתתף באופן פעיל במאמצי ארגונים יהודיים להקים מדינה יהודית עצמאית בפלשתינה.
claims.quote: he participated actively in various Jewish organizations' efforts to create an independent Jewish state in Palestine.

claims.text: לפי אתר, האפקין תרם את כל רכושו וכן 300,000 דולר לקרן לעידוד כישרונות צעירים בבתי ספר דתיים יהודיים במזרח אירופה.
claims.quote: He donated all his property, as well as $ 300,000, to the Foundation for the Promotion of Young Talents of the Jewish Religious Schools of Eastern Europe.

claims.text: לפי מילון הביוגרפיה המדעית, האפקין מת בלוזאן ב-25 באוקטובר 1930.
claims.quote: (b. Odessa, Russia, 15 March 1860; d. Lausanne, Switzerland, 25 October 1930)

claims.text: לפי קייב פוסט, האפקין מת בלוזאן ב-26 באוקטובר 1930 בחדר מלון.
claims.quote: so a year later he moved to Lausanne, where he died on October 26, 1930, in a hotel room

claims.text: לפי ה-BBC, במרץ 1902 מתו במולקוואל 19 איש מטטנוס לאחר החיסון.
claims.quote: In March 1902, in the village of Mulkowel in Punjab, 19 people died from tetanus after being inoculated with Haffkine's vaccine.

claims.text: לפי הוגוד, כל המתים קיבלו חיסון מבקבוק אחד, 53N, שיצא ממעבדת בומביי 26 יום קודם.
claims.quote: all the dead had received vaccine from one bottle labelled 53N, issued from the Plague laboratory in Bombay 26 days previously

claims.text: 88 האנשים האחרים שקיבלו חיסון מבקבוקים אחרים לא נפגעו.
claims.quote: and that the other 88 people who had received vaccine from other bottles were unaffected

claims.text: לפי מילון הביוגרפיה המדעית, האפקין הושעה ללא שכר עוד לפני שהחלו חקירות מסודרות.
claims.quote: Haffkine was suspended without pay before proper investigations were even begun.

claims.text: ועדת החקירה בראשות הנשיא ג'נקינס לא כללה בקטריולוגים כלל.
claims.quote: A Commission of Inquiry was appointed, headed by Sir Lawrence Jenkins, chief justice of Bombay. None of its members were bacteriologists.

claims.text: הוועדה גילתה שהאפקין שינה את נוהלי הייצור שנבדקו ואושרו בעבר על ידי ועדת הדבר.
claims.quote: the Commission became aware that Haffkine had changed the production procedures that had been examined and approved by the Plague Commis- sion

claims.text: הוועדה ראתה בהשמטת החומצה הקרבולית חומרה קיצונית.
claims.quote: The Commission viewed the omission of carbolic acid with extreme gravity

claims.text: עוזר המזריק במולקוואל הפיל את המלקחיים על הקרקע ולא עיקר אותם כהלכה לפני פתיחת הבקבוק.
claims.quote: Narindar Singh, the assistant who opened the vaccine bottles, dropped the forceps on the ground as the stopper moved in the bottle

claims.text: רונלד רוס יחד עם סימפסון פתחו בקמפיין לטהר את האפקין מאשמה באסון.
claims.quote: Ross, together with Simpson, commenced a campaign to exonerate Haffkine from blame for the disaster.

claims.text: שיא הקמפיין היה מכתב ל'טיימס' ב-29 ביולי 1907, עליו חתמו עשרה בקטריולוגים בולטים.
claims.quote: The climax of the campaign to exonerate Haffkine came in a letter to The Times published on 29 July 1907 that was signed by 10 distinguished bacter- iologists

claims.text: רוס כתב ב'נייצ'ר' ב-1907 שהאשמת המעבדה גרמה לדחיית החיסון בידי העם, ואולי לאובדן אלפי חיים מהדבר.
claims.quote: caused, I have been told, a sudden and wholesale rejection of the invaluable vaccine by the people, with the probable result that thousands of lives may have been lost from plague

claims.text: רוס כתב שאם המצב לא יתוקן, הדבר יוכיח את אדישות הודו ושליטיה למדע ואת כפיות הטובה כלפי אחד מגדולי מיטיביהם.
claims.quote: it will convict India and her rulers of indifference to science, stupidity, injustice, and gross ingratitude to one of their greatest benefactors

claims.text: לאחר טיהורו חזר האפקין להודו כמנהל ראשי של המעבדה הביולוגית בקלקוטה.
claims.quote: he gladly returned as director in chief of the Calcutta Biological Laboratory

claims.text: לאחר חזרתו נאסר עליו לבצע ניסויים, והוא הוגבל למחקר תיאורטי.
claims.quote: he was barred from carrying out any trials, limiting him to theoretical research

claims.text: לפי ה-BBC, ב-1914 בגיל 55 פרש האפקין מהשירות האזרחי ההודי ועזב את המדינה.
claims.quote: In 1914, aged 55, Haffkine retired from the Indian Civil Service and left the country.

claims.text: לפי מילון הביוגרפיה המדעית, ב-1915 הגיע לגיל פרישת חובה ועזב את הודו.
claims.quote: In 1915 he reached compulsory retirement age and left India

claims.text: לפי אתר, האפקין היה קורבן לאנטישמיות מספר פעמים בחייו, מרוסיה הצארית ועד עבודתו בהודו הבריטית.
claims.quote: Haffkine was a victim of anti-Semitism several times in his life, from his early days in Tsarist Russia to his days of work

claims.text: לפי אלי צ'רנין, לא ניכר מהארכיונים שהאפקין היה קורבן גלוי לאנטישמיות.
claims.quote: was not evident from the archives that Haffkine was overtly victimized by anti-Semitism

claims.text: לפי מילון הביוגרפיה המדעית, בתוך שנתיים חוסנו 45,000 איש והתמותה מכולרה ירדה ב-70 אחוזים.
claims.quote: Within the two years 45,000 persons were inoculated, most of them twice, and the death rate from cholera was reduced by 70 percent.

claims.text: לפי המאמר של הוגוד, בבית הכלא בביקולה חוסנו 154 אסירים שהתנדבו.
claims.quote: Haffkine arranged to inoculate 154 prison- ers who volunteered. Three of the inoculated men died that day

claims.text: לפי ה-BBC, בבית הכלא בביקולה חיסן האפקין 147 אסירים והשאיר 172 ללא טיפול.
claims.quote: He inoculated 147 prisoners and left 172 untreated.

claims.text: לפי ה-BBC, בקבוק 53N הוכן 41 יום קודם במעבדת פראל.
claims.quote: All the evidence appeared to point to a fatal contamination of bottle 53N - prepared 41 days earlier at the Parel lab.

claims.text: ניסיון קודם של פראן בוולנסיה לחסן נגד כולרה לא אומץ במדינות אחרות, והופסק בספרד.
